topic: Hydraulic rock breaker — operation, oversize handling, and operator technique
title: Hydraulic rock breaker — operation, oversize handling, and operator technique
body: Every hour the breaker spends blank-firing or prying boulders is an hour closer to a seized piston, a cracked tool, or a bent excavator stick — and a tool that dies in days instead of months means oversize backs up at the crusher or the loading face until someone's standing idle waiting on it.
keyPoints: Breaker is for breaking rock only — not lifting, not sweeping, not prying material loose. Use the lower housing to move boulders.
Stop the instant the rock breaks. Blank firing — idle strokes after the break, or prying that lifts the piston off the tool — is the single biggest cause of hammer failure.
90° working angle, feed along the tool axis, max 15 seconds in one spot before stone dust dampens the impact and deforms the tip.
Never fire with the boom, stick, or bucket cylinder fully retracted or fully extended — that's structural damage to the excavator, not just the tool.
Stop immediately on excessive hose vibration (punctured accumulator) or visible hydraulic oil along the shaft (seal failure) — workshop job, not a field fix.
apply: Watch the hammer operators at the ROM pad and loading face for the "let it fall through and idle-strike" habit — it's the fastest way to turn a good tool into next week's workshop backlog.
